 2.0 BACKGROUND & OPERATIONAL NEED 

 In accordance with  Section 708 of Public Law 114-328 ,  DoD Instruction (DoDI) 1322.24  ( Medical Readiness Training , Change 1), and  Air Force Surgeon General (AF/SG) Directives , the Department of the Air Force has formally standardized battlefield trauma care under the  Joint Trauma System (JTS)  and the  Committee on Tactical Combat Casualty Care (CoTCCC) , fully sundowning the legacy Self-Aid and Buddy Care (SABC) program. 

 Historical execution of TCCC across Alaska installations utilizing fragmented, collateral-duty military instructors has led to instructional variances, scheduling backlogs, and readiness inspection findings. The Government requires a turnkey, enterprise commercial solution to provide fully certified, standardized TCCC instruction, high-fidelity trauma simulation, mobile training capability, and authoritative database reporting. 

 
	  Base Performance Requirement:  Permanent, turnkey instruction and simulation support at  Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson (JBER)  in Southcentral Alaska. 
	  Optional Performance Requirement:  Mobile Training Team (MTT) instructional rotations and simulation transport to  Eielson Air Force Base (EAFB)  in Interior Alaska, exercisable at the Government's discretion based on operational requirements and funding availability. 
 

 3.0 SCOPE OF REQUIREMENT & BASIC DETAILS 

  3.1 Supported Organizations by Structure  

 Core / Base Requirement (JBER): 

 
	  673d Air Base Wing (673 ABW) & 673d Medical Group (673 MDG)  – JBER (Active Duty) 
	  176th Wing (176 WG)  – JBER (Alaska Air National Guard, including 212th Rescue Squadron) 
	  477th Fighter Group (477 FG)  – JBER (Air Force Reserve Command) 
 

 Optional Requirement (Eielson AFB): 

 
	  354th Fighter Wing (354 FW) & 354th Medical Group (354 MDG)  – Eielson AFB (Active Duty PACAF) 
	  168th Wing (168 WG)  – Eielson AFB (Alaska Air National Guard) 
 

  3.2 Required Training Tiers & Curricula  

 All training must utilize current, standardized JTS terminal and enabling learning objectives published via Deployed Medicine across four distinct skill tiers: 

 
	  Tier 1: All Service Members (ASM):  8 contact hours; baseline survivability for non-medical personnel (tourniquets, wound packing, pressure dressings, airway positioning, hypothermia mitigation). 
	  Tier 2: Combat Lifesaver (CLS):  40 contact hours; advanced non-medical tactical responder care (needle decompression, vented chest seals, basic analgesia, casualty collection point operations, MIST/9-Line reporting). 
	  Tier 3: Combat Medic / Corpsman (CMC) & Medic-X:  64 contact hours; clinical field trauma for 4N0X1 aerospace medical technicians and AFMS MTF clinicians (bougie-assisted surgical cricothyroidotomy, supraglottic airways, intraosseous access, TXA administration, blood transfusions). 
	  Tier 4: Combat Paramedic / Provider (CPP):  80 contact hours; advanced pre-hospital trauma for Special Warfare (PJ/Combat Rescue Officers), flight surgeons, and independent duty medical technicians. 
	  TCCC Refresher Training:  8–16 contact hours tailored skills sustainment (non-certifying per DoDI 1322.24 § 4.3).
